daily.summary: Norwegian energy company Equinor is containing a cyberattack on its IT systems that disrupted staff access to internal services, though it says oil and gas production was not affected and no attacker has been named. The FBI issued alerts on an AI framework used to automate intrusions and on a $400 million North Korean crypto-theft scheme, and Google described a Russian FSB-linked group impersonating one US victim's staff to breach another. CISA flagged active exploitation of a critical Perforce Puppet flaw and urged patching of the Java4Shell bug, while newly disclosed Copeland refrigeration controller flaws are already being probed.

weekly.summary: The week's reporting centres on attackers using AI to speed up intrusions: the FBI, Google and Unit 42 all describe autonomous attack frameworks in real operations. State-linked activity includes North Korean financial theft, Russian espionage against Romanian government email and against two US organizations, and a reported China-linked intrusion at a European telecom provider. Equinor's IT outage is the week's most notable incident at an allied energy operator, with production reported unaffected, and patching pressure is high across Java, Puppet, Cisco BroadWorks and refrigeration controllers.
